note: Every scored submission whose OFFLINE number is our own ruler on our own members. The prose ledger is comp/SUBMISSIONS.md; these are the same numbers in the form something can read. Mixed fusions are excluded - their offline column says 'mixed' because published members were fitted elsewhere. Entries that returned no score, and the 0.500 kit failures, are excluded: they measure the kit, not the recipe.

SCOPE is the denominator, and it is the reason two entries here are not orderable against the rest. An ENSEMBLE number is the holdout AUC of the thing that was submitted. A MEMBER_MEAN is the average of its members' individual holdouts, which is systematically LOWER than the ensemble it describes, so comparing one against the other reads the averaging as a quality difference. Two rows carry the words 'holdout mean' in the ledger and are marked member_mean; two more are recorded as a bare number with no statement of which, and are marked unknown rather than guessed.

READ WITHIN member_mean (--scope member_mean, 2026-08-16): 4 entries, 5 orderable pairs, and BOTH pairs the holdout resolves are inverted - trained_v3 and trained_v5 carry member means 0.021 ABOVE trained_v2 and scored 0.006 BELOW it. Confounded, and the confound is the point: trained_v2 5 members are five FOLDS, so together they saw all the training data, while v3 and v5 hold 2-3 members of one split. On the ensemble scope the count runs the other way (trained_v8, 5 members of one split, 0.911 against efficient_v4 2 members, 0.919), so what these two readings agree on is that member COUNT is not the axis - training-data COVERAGE is. Not actionable here: folds are out of scope by the owner's standing constraint. Recorded so the count reading is not mistaken for a diversity result.

MEMBERS_NAMED is the field that makes a row rebuildable and priceable, and 31 of the 48 entries were written without it - which left `Champion.from_board` raising a bare KeyError on the top of the board and left `unpriceable()` inert on exactly the all-data rows it exists for. Five were recovered on 2026-08-24 and twelve more on 2026-08-25, in both cases by parsing the `chosen` tuple out of the entry's own kernel script with `ast` and asserting the tuple's LENGTH against the `members` count the row already carried independently - all seventeen matched. Two more were recovered on 2026-08-25 (chosen_v2, onedecode_v2) and the REASON the rest resist recovery was corrected at the same time. The earlier recovery joined a row to a script through the row's own `kernel` field, so a row whose `kernel` was null was never offered a script at all - and that is a different thing from having none. Joining on the entry's NAME instead (`chosen_v2` -> `comp/kernels/kneemri-chosen`) finds a surviving script for THIRTEEN of the fourteen; only fusion25_v2 has no directory. So `no script survives` was true of one row and asserted of fourteen. What actually blocks the other eleven is the SELECTION STYLE, not the script's absence: they call `KernelRun(members=N)`, which is `strongest(N)` over recorded holdouts, and a rank evaluated against a package that has since changed cannot be replayed by parsing. chosen_v2 and onedecode_v2 name their members literally (`names=`, one through a local variable that `KernelScript._strings` already follows), both tuples match the `members` count the row carried independently, and both were read from the AS-SUBMITTED commit dba7719 rather than from HEAD - which matters, because `kneemri-chosen` was edited on 2026-08-17 after the entry shipped. The tuple was unchanged by that edit; it is checked rather than assumed, since the sixfresh caveat above is exactly this hazard. A THIRD row was recovered in the same pass and it failed for neither reason: weakseven_v1 carried `kernel` AND a surviving named tuple, and was missed because its `members_named` was an EMPTY LIST rather than an absent key. That is the worse of the two spellings - a consumer asking `'members_named' in row` reads it as recovered while one asking for truthiness reads it as missing, so it answered the earlier sweep's question with the wrong half. Its seven names were read from a32866c, the commit that shipped it, and match the `members` count. ABSENT, NEVER EMPTY is the rule for this field. The remaining twelve are left absent rather than filled from prose. One caveat on the recovered set: sixfresh_v1 and sixfresh_v2 share the one kernel directory `kneemri-sixfresh`, so both carry the tuple that directory holds NOW - they record the same six members and the same 0.931, which is consistent with a re-run, but an edit in place between the two submissions would be invisible here.
